Commentary.Commentary: Right! We are done and dusted with this. Zimbabwe are effectively out of the running to make it to the final as they don't have a single point on the board after three games. So, Pakistan and Australia will face off for the trophy. But, before that, they will take on each other on 5th July in the 5th game of the tri-series. It begins at 1000 local (0800 GMT). Do join in for that. Cheers!

Sarfraz Ahmed, the winning captain, sounds very unhappy with Pakistan's bowling performance. He states that since his batters gave them a good start, they could overhaul the target. Says that the upcoming game against Australia is a dress rehearsal before the finals, in which they'll look to do well.

Hamilton Masakadza, the losing skipper, is happy with the fight shown by his team mates, although they lost the game. States that they ended up 15-20 runs short and also opines that their fielding let them down. Feels hopeful of doing better in the coming game. Opines that since they don't get many international games, they need to do well in whatever opportunities that they get.

Solomon Mire is adjudged the Man of the Match for his knock of 94. He says that it was a good day for him and hence the shots came off. Concedes that the gameplan for them was that at least one in the top three need to stay long and take the game deep. States that he had been struggling for a while in recent times with the ball and hence is good to get a few overs under his belt.

Zimbabwe needed wickets to win this game. Mire and Musakanda gave them a fighting chance with the total they had on the board, but the bowlers couldn't back it up. The Powerplay more or less ended it for them, because post that, the Pakistan batsmen never needed to take any risks and went about their business without any trouble. Also, the captaincy, maybe, lacked some aggression, as Pakistan were allowed to rotate strike without any pressure. It was an improved performance from them, but just wasn't enough. Plenty to still work on obviously. Presentation follows...

A comfortable enough victory for the Men in Green. Had 5 balls to spare. It all began with the start Zaman and Sohail provided them. That pretty much put the visiting side in pole position to win this game as the asking rate was always in control after that and the batsmen to follow had their jobs made easy for them. Solid partnerships from the middle order, which included the likes of Talat, Sarfraz and Malik, saw the match through with utmost ease.

FOUR! And that's the game. PAKISTAN WIN BY 7 WICKETS! Easily done by the Pakistan skipper. Length delivery around off, Sarfraz cuts it late as he plays it down to third man. Beats the keeper and short third man, finding the fence with ease.
Tried to finish it off with a boundary. Length ball around off, Malik looks to loft it over the off side but can't connect.
Taps it away on the off side with gentle hands and collects a quick single.
FOUR! Shot. Full delivery outside the line of off stump, Sarfraz lofts it over covers and sends it across the rope for a boundary.

Some sloppy work and a faint chance of a run out - that's what! Sarfraz drives it down to long on and takes a single. The throw comes in to Blessing who misfields and seeing this, the batsmen decide to steal another run. The keeper collects the ball and throws it to the bowler, who takes the bails off. Shoaib Malik, however, made it back in with ease.
There's a bit of confusion. What happened there?
Fired in full on off stump, Sarfraz digs it out towards mid-wicket. In the gap and some quick running enables the batsmen to two a couple of runs.
Full toss outside off, Malik walks down the track and flicks it towards square leg. Chisoro stationed there misfields which allows the batsmen to change ends.
Cuts this away nicely through point and gets a single. 14 needed off 12 balls.
FOUR! Terrific shot! Shoaib Malik dances down the track to this length delivery and goes across the line. Over mid-wicket and he bisects the gap between the two men in the deep. Boundary results.
Good running between the wickets. Malik pushes this towards long on and takes the fielder on. Beats him too as he comes back for the second in a jiffy.
FOUR! Wastes no time to get going. Off the mark with a boundary. Short ball, Malik makes room and slaps this towards third man. Hits it square enough to beat the fielder and get it across the rope.
Shoaib Malik is the new man in.

OUT! Got 'em! Seems this was the plan all along. It's worked, albeit after conceding two extra runs. Full and wide again outside off, Talat goes after it this time and gets it off the outer half. it goes flies towards point where Zhuwao moves a little to his right and takes a sharp catch. A good knock from Talat comes to an end, he's done the job for his side, even if he's missed out on his fifty.
Wide! Similar delivery, outside off and across the tramline, wide signalled.
Wide! Comes from around the wicket and darts it too far outside off. Wide signalled.
Length delivery outside off, punched from within the crease through to sweeper cover for one.
Chris Mpofu back on.
Length ball going across, Talat swings and there's a noise as the ball goes behind. The keeper appeals, but the bowler doesn't seem as interested. Dot ball to end the over.
Fuller around off, Talat throws the kitchen sink at it, only to get a thick edge down to third man. A double is collected.
Shortish in length, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.

It keeps a little low as Blessing bowls the off cutter on a back of a length, which is it takes the inner edge onto the pads as Sarfraz looks to swing across the line. He wanted the run, but was sent back by Talat. For some reason, he's annoyed with Hussain. Not sure why, because the run was never on.
Brings out the short one and bangs it in short, Sarfraz attempts to play the ramp shot but fails to make connection.
Speared full, well outside off, Talat gets low, opens the face and squeezes it out to third man for a run.
Blessing Muzarabani into the attack once more.
Full ball, lofted towards long on on a couple of bounce for a single. 32 needed in 24.
Floated delivery close to the off stick, Talat lofts it down long on. Sarfraz takes off quickly for the first, calls for the second and makes sure Hussain responds fast. Good running.

Good stop from Hamilton once again. Talat comes forward to this tossed up ball outside off and drills it to the covers. The skipper there moves swiftly to his right, slides and makes an excellent stop.
Places this square through point and gets to the other end.

FOUR! There's the deft touch again. Nicely done. Outside off, with some turn and bounce, Sarfraz Ahmed waits for it, plays it late with a slightly open face and gets it past short third man. Once that happened, the ball was always going to win the race.
The batsman plays the pull shot. They pick up a single.
Tendai Chisoro called back on to bowl.
Full and outside off, Sarfraz fails to connect with the cover drive.
FOUR! Deft! Cleverly done. Spinning away from around off, Ahmed plays it late and dabs it past the keeper, across the third man fence for a boundary.
Controls the pull behind square leg and takes one.

Dropped! But that's just a technicality. Too harsh to call it a dropped. Stunning effort from the Zimbabwean captain. Sarfraz comes ahead and drives it in the air towards extra cover. Hamilton there dives full stretch to his left, gets a hand to it but can't hold on. Saves a certain boundary for his side for sure. Single taken.
A fumble from Mire allows the batsmen to take an extra run. Sarfraz works it through mid-wicket and takes one. Solomon fumbles while picking it up and hence the batsmen come back for the second.

FOUR! Another boundary. This is good batting from the Pakistan skipper. Sees the flight on the ball and that it's landing full, Sarfraz kneels down and sweeps it behind square leg, beating the man in the deep.
Wellington Masakadza called back into the attack.
Hussain Talat works this with soft hands through mid-wicket. Big gap out there, smart work, will get two by the time the man in the deep gets to the ball.

Chance of a run out! Had he hit, would have been real close. Sarfraz drops it down in front of point and takes off. The fielder rushes to the ball quickly and fires a throw at the striker's end but misses. Wasn't too far away though.
FOUR! Well, guess that answers why. Good call at the end it seems. Length delivery from the bowler, Sarfraz goes across the line and lofts it over mid-wicket to find the fence.

That was in the air for a long while but fell short. Talat made room and lofted the full ball outside off over point. Didn't connect well at all, but luckily for him it fell in no man's land. Just a single was taken though, for some strange reason. Seems it was Sarfraz's call.
Fraction straight in line, nudged fine down the leg side for a run.
Wide! Mire comes steaming in and darts it too far outside off, Sarfraz tries to connect but fails to do so. It's across the other side of the tramline so the umpire signals a wide.
Fuller in length, in line of the stumps, flicked away in the gap on the leg side for a single. The 100 comes up for Pakistan.
Short and wide outside off, cut square towards point to end the over.
Slightly quicker through the air and attacking the stumps, drilled down to long on for one more.
The skipper is off the mark here. Sarfraz comes forward and knocks it down to long on for one run.
Around off, Talat without much foot movement pushes this through the covers and gets to the other end.
Slower through the air, around off, Hussain taps this just beside him with soft hands.
From around the wicket, it's floated on the stumps, Talat blocks with a straight blade.
Tendai Chisoro will bowl again.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. The batsmen have run through for a single. End of a good over from Mire.
Stays inside his crease and keeps it out rather safely.
Sarfraz Ahmed makes his way to the middle next.

OUT! Solomon Mire can do no wrong today! Could this be the turning point in this game? The moment which could fire Zimbabwe up? Fuller in length on the stumps, Zaman looks to clear long on but doesn't connect well at all. Skies it in the mid on region where Mpofu comes running from mid off. Mire was going back himself but Chris was there first. Settled under the ball well and took a very good catch. The dangerous southpaw departs just shy of his fifty. Pakistan need 68 to win off 50 balls.
Back of a length moving across, outside off, Zaman works it towards point and wants a run. Takes off but is sent back in time as the fielder got to the ball rather quickly.
Opens the face of the bat, dabs this square on the off side and takes a single.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Talat easily picks it up and places it through square leg. The fielder in the deep cuts it off and keeps the batsmen down to two.
Solomon Mire comes on to bowl. Did extremely well with the bat, can he replicate something similar with the ball?
Flatter around middle and leg, Zaman made room to play it through the off side, but was cramped for room. Ends up pushing it down the track.
Hussain lets it come to him and directs it towards square leg for a single.
Another couple, this time after flicking it through square leg.
Two, two, two, shouts Talat as soon as he lofts this one towards wide long on. Before Mire gets to his left and fires the throw, a couple is taken.
Loopy outside off, a single milked down to long off.
Slower through the air on the pads, Talat plays it with soft hands towards square leg for one.
This one is turned through square leg for another single.
SIX! Short, punished. Waller bowls a half-tracker around leg, sliding down. Talat kneels and pulls it over backward square leg for a maximum.
Third couple on the trot. This one is whipped through mid-wicket for another two. The running has been good between these two.
Good effort in the deep. This one is lofted over wide mid off. The man from long off gets to his right and keeps it in play. A couple results.
Tossed up outside off, lofted over covers for a brace.
Flatter in trajectory in line of the stumps, FZ works it through mid-wicket for one. He moves to 4 runs short of a fifty.
Short in length, pulled away through mid-wicket for one. 92 more needed off 66.
Delivered wide from the crease, Masakadza fires it wide outside off seeing Zaman bakc away. The southpaw fails to reach it.
Floated around middle, flicked away through mid-wicket for one.
Poor work! This delivery is pulled through backward square leg. With Zhuwao in the deep, it should've been just one. But he lets it through and concedes another one.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
On the pads, turned away through square leg for one.
Short in length outside off, Zaman hangs back and cuts it straight to backward point.

This one is nicely looped up in line of the stumps, Talat whips it away through mid-wicket. He wanted a second and set off for it, but spotting the fielder get to the ball, Zaman denied him the same. Hussain somehow made his way back, but then the fielder in the deep couldn't collect the ball in a go. Just a single results in the end.
Waller sees Fakhar come down the track and serves this wider. Zaman reaches out to it and gets it through covers for one.
Fired quicker outside off, Zaman looks to cut it but misses. Moor takes it and whips the bails off in a flash but the Pakistan southpaw's back foot went nowhere out.
Tossed up around off, Talat drives it inside out down to long off for a single.
Flatter one from round the wicket, Zaman goes back and slaps it through point for one.
More spin. Malcolm Waller is introduced to the bowling crease.
Tossed up around leg, flicked away through square leg for a single. A decent start for Wellington.
Fired on the pads, worked away through square leg for one.
Flatter around middle and leg, pushed through mid on for one.
Floated around off, defended to the off side off the front foot.
Hussain Talat walks in at no.3 for Pakistan.

OUT! The youngster gets the desired breakthrough for the hosts. He is successful in breaking the 58-run opening stand of Pakistan. Wellington Masakadza tosses this one up from round the wicket, Haris Sohail dances down the track to hit it straight over. But he ends up dragging it aerially. The ball travels straight to Solomon Mire at long on, who makes no mistake.
Begins with a slower delivery from round the wicket, Sohail looks to defend. The outside edge is taken and a brace results as the ball rolls towards third man.
Wellington Masakadza to have a bowl now.
Angling in on a length, worked away through square leg to retain strike. Pakistan finish on 56/0 at the end of the Powerplay.
Good running! Very full outside off, squeezed towards short third man. But even though the ball went straight to Chisoro there, the pair stole a run.
This ball is punched off the back foot through the cover region for one.

In the air but safe! Short in length from round the wicket, Zaman pulls it powerfully. The ball flies towards fine leg and lands just short of Muzarabani there. He did well to stop that and keep it down to one.
Fuller around off, flicked away through wide mid on for another single.
Short ball around off, pulled away to the on side for one.
Back over the wicket, Fakhar pushes it towards covers to retain strike. The 50 is raised for Pakistan as well as this new opening pair for them.
Whooo! That might sting. Muzarabani comes round the wicket and bangs it short, seeing Zaman charge down. The southpaw goes with the pull but ends up getting it off the glove.
Blessing drags his length back, Zaman pulls it in front of square on the leg side for a brace.
On the pads on a fuller length, clipped away through mid-wicket for one.
WIDE! Full and down the leg side, HS misses the flick.
Short in length, pulled away through square leg for one.
FOUR! Length ball angling away, Fakhar stands tall and punches it through covers for a boundary. The runs are continuing to flow for Pakistan.
Blessing Muzarabani gets a change of ends.
Full outside off, driven towards long off for one.
Fuller around off and middle, Sohail looks to tuck it away but ends up getting it off the inner half towards fine leg. He wanted a couple but quick work in the deep denies him that opportunity.
WIDE! Harsh? Maybe. This is full and outside off, Sohail makes room initially and hence fails to reach that one. Seems to be a good dot ball but then the umpire stretches both his arms.
Once again, a delivery in line of the stumps is worked away to the on side for one.
WIDE! Full and down the leg side, Zaman gets inside the line but misses the hoick.
Back of a length outside off, Zaman looks to make room and smash it. Misses the ball as it bounced high over.
This one is tucked away through mid-wicket for one.
Mpofu comes round the wicket and lands it outside off. Zaman pushes it towards point and sets off for a run. There is a wild shy at the bowler's end but the batter makes it in.
Chris Mpofu to have a go with the ball now.

Confusion, but no harm done! Sohail turns it towards square leg and wants a run. Hamilton Masakadza gets to the ball in a bid to fire a throw to the keeper but fails to collect it. Meanwhile, the batters were ball watching and hence couldn't take a run.
Quicker through the air this time, pushed towards covers for one.
FOUR! Tossed up around leg, Zaman kneels down and slog sweeps it through square leg. The man from deep mid-wicket tries to stop that getting to his left but in vain.
This one is punched down to long off for another run.
Flatter around off, pushed through mid off for one.

SIX! Massive! Loopy ball from round the wicket, Zaman charges down the track and absolutely belts it over the bowler's head for half a dozen. The on-air commentators also talk about the fact that there is no necessity to bowl a spinner with the fielding restrictions on, specially when he does the job for you when the field spreads.
FOUR! Wonderful stroke to end the over! This is full and angling away, Sohail just lofts it over mid off and earns himself a boundary.
Fuller on the pads, turned through backward square leg for a couple.
On a length in line of the stumps, Sohail stands tall and defends.
Fuller this time, defended from the crease with a straight bat.
Length ball on the hips, worked away through square leg for one.
On a length in line of the stumps, blocked from the crease.
Blessing Muzarabani to run in with the new ball from the other end.
Shorter in length, pulled down to long on for one. 13 off the opening over, as opposed to 12 that Zimbabwe got.
FOUR! Tossed up on middle and leg, Zaman kneels and plays the sweep through square leg. The ball trickles away to the fence.

FOUR! First boundary of the innings. This one is fired full, outside off. Zaman squeezes it out. He manages to get it in the gap between backward point and short third man. This time, although Mire puts in a spirited chase from the former position, he fails to prevent the boundary.
Flatter on the pads, flicked away through mid-wicket for one.

Well done, Muzarabani! Fakhar stays deep in the crease and just chips the pull in the gap between backward square leg and short fine leg. Blessing chases it down from the latter position and does well to save a run for his side. It is taken upstairs for a check and all's fine.
Flatter from round the wicket, Zaman goes back and pulls it back towards the bowler.

Welcome back! With 163 to get, Fakhar Zaman and Haris Sohail walk out to open the batting for Pakistan. Tendai Chisoro will have a go with the ball first up. He had a very good outing in Zimbabwe's previous game, keeping in mind the carnage that was on show.
